government.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
government.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

government.title: Social Norms, State Punishment, and Motivation Crowding in Anti‐Corruption Messaging: Experimental Evidence From China
government.short_title: Social Norms, State Punishment, and Motivation Crowding in Anti‐Corruption Messaging: Experime…
government.source: Governance
government.plain_summary: This study examines how people's beliefs about corruption influence their attitudes towards fighting it. In a large survey experiment conducted in China, researchers found that when people were told the actual level of tolerance for corruption is much lower than they thought, it made them more likely to want to fight corruption. However, if this information was paired with suggestions of punishment, it seemed to weaken the effect. This shows that simply telling people about how corrupt others are might not be as effective as also showing what actions can be taken against it.

government.title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Public Rights
government.short_title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Pu…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how governments in Iran handle situations where their actions harm collective interests or public rights. It examines legal systems that provide ways to compensate for such harms and restore balance. The research finds there are different types of compensation depending on whether the government acted wrongfully or not, and it also covers cases where they did something lawful but still caused damage. Challenges like unclear laws, difficulty proving harm in collective situations, and lack of coordination between different parts of the system can make these mechanisms less effective even if the basic rules are clear.

government.short_title: A Qualitative Analysis of Administrative Transparency Requirements in Government Construction…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how governments should make their construction contract processes more transparent to prevent inefficiencies and corruption. It covers all stages from deciding what to build to evaluating its success. Transparency isn't just about sharing information; it also means having clear rules, fair procedures, and being able to prove decisions were right. The court's rulings on this matter help enforce transparency as a legal requirement.

government.title: The Dual Impact of International Sanctions and FATF Requirements on the Independence and Effectiveness of Government Financial Supervision in Iran’s Public Law System
government.short_title: The Dual Impact of International Sanctions and FATF Requirements on the Independence and Effec…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: Financial supervision in Iran faces significant challenges due to both international sanctions and FATF requirements. These pressures affect how government institutions manage resources and ensure transparency. Sanctions limit access to data and cooperation with other countries, while FATF standards promote more formal procedures for oversight but also increase compliance costs. This creates a complex environment where institutions can gain technical tools but lose their independence due to external constraints like sanctions.

government.title: The Role of Government Structure in the Emergence of Crimes Against Humanity
government.short_title: The Role of Government Structure in the Emergence of Crimes Against Humanity
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: The study found that certain government structures can facilitate crimes against humanity by concentrating power in authoritarian regimes, allowing discriminatory ideologies to dominate, causing crises in legitimacy, or implementing unfair economic policies. These factors weaken checks on violence, legitimize harmful actions, suppress opposition groups, and cause harm to specific populations. To prevent such crimes, it's important for governments to strengthen the rule of law, ensure judicial independence, expand democratic oversight, and promote human rights values within their systems.

government.title: Evaluation of the Policymaking System and Institutions for Combating Administrative Corruption in Afghanistan during the Republican Period (2004–2021)
government.short_title: Evaluation of the Policymaking System and Institutions for Combating Administrative Corruption…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: During the Republican period in Afghanistan (2004-2021), administrative corruption was a major issue affecting governance. The government worked with international support to create laws, anti-corruption strategies, and institutions. However, despite progress in these areas, corruption did not significantly decrease. The study found that while there were improvements in legislation and institution building, the effectiveness of policies weakened at implementation stages.

government.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
government.short_title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Inte…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This research evaluates Iran's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to see how well it supports responsible use of AI. The strategy emphasizes values like human dignity and national priorities, but lacks clear plans for key areas like funding, data access, and regulation. To succeed, the strategy needs more specific details on these aspects. Practitioners should focus not just on ethical principles, but also on practical steps to ensure AI is used responsibly and effectively in Iran.

government.title: Challenges of Environmental Governance in Iraq and Strategies for Its Strengthening Based on Sustainable Development Standards
government.short_title: Challenges of Environmental Governance in Iraq and Strategies for Its Strengthening Based on S…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: Iraq faces significant challenges in managing its environment due to structural, legal, institutional, and security issues that harm public health, resources, and social stability. Despite having laws and international commitments, Iraq's environmental governance system is ineffective. To improve this, reforms are needed on multiple fronts including strengthening legislation, empowering institutions, integrating environmental concerns into economic policies, and enhancing regional and international cooperation. Aligning with sustainable development principles like good governance, stakeholder participation, and accountability can help address these issues and pave the way for Iraq's sustainable future.

government.title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Official Channels: A Critical Analysis of the 2013 Anti‑Smuggling Law and Its 2021 Amendments
government.short_title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Of…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: The smuggling of goods and currency through official channels in Iran remains a significant issue despite various laws enacted over the years. While there have been efforts like the 2013 Anti-Smuggling Law and subsequent amendments, this practice has not decreased but may have worsened in some areas such as reverse smuggling and organized currency trafficking. This article examines how well these laws balance different goals like prevention, repression, rehabilitation, and compensation. It found that while there are positive changes, the law still faces major issues including a broad definition of smuggling, multiple bodies leading to lengthy proceedings, disproportionate penalties, and weak enforcement due to corruption.

government.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
government.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
government.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
government.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

government.title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities of Nigeria
government.short_title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities…
government.source: RUDN Journal of Public Administration
government.plain_summary: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) was implemented in 2015 to centralize public funds and improve transparency and accountability in Nigerian federal universities, but financial irregularities still occur. This study found that TSA has improved transparency and accountability significantly (p=0.004), but also faces challenges like bureaucratic delays and actors circumventing the system. Corruption persists as it transforms into less traceable forms. Despite savings of over 10 trillion Naira nationally, corruption perception scores remain low.

government.title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary After Indonesian Constitutional Court Decision No. 66/PUU-XXIV/2026: A Fiqh Siyasah Perspective
government.short_title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary…
government.source: JISRev: Journal of Islamic Studies Review
government.plain_summary: This research looks at the difference between maladministration and corruption, using a specific case about buying Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia. It found four key factors to decide if something is corruption: whether someone intended to do wrong, if they got personal benefit from it, if money was lost as a result, and if proper steps were taken afterward. The study also suggests that when all these factors are met, what started as maladministration can be considered corruption. However, the research points out there should be an initial check by a special committee before going to criminal courts.

government.short_title: Fighting Corruption and Transparency of Political Parties Finances as Prerequisites of the EU’…
government.source: Analele Universității din Oradea. Seria: Relații Internaționale și Studii Europene
government.plain_summary: In Republic of Moldova, corruption continues to be a significant issue affecting democratic governance. Political party financing is a key area where corruption often occurs, leading to clientelism, influence from oligarchs, and state capture. The article looks at how Moldova has improved its laws to make political party funding more transparent, but also highlights ongoing challenges. To meet the requirements for EU accession, it's crucial to enforce these laws better, improve verification systems, and ensure public funding strengthens the link between parties and citizens.

government.title: UNIVERSAL INTERNATIONAL LEGAL MECHANISMS OF ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICY IN THE CONSTRUCTION SECTOR
government.short_title: UNIVERSAL INTERNATIONAL LEGAL MECHANISMS OF ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICY IN THE CONSTRUCTION SECTOR
government.source: Metaverse Science, Society and Law
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how anti-corruption policies in the construction sector are shaped by international laws and organizations like the United Nations, OECD, and World Bank. It examines how these international bodies create rules and implement them to fight corruption. The goal is to help Ukraine improve its own anti-corruption policies by using these international standards. By doing this, Ukraine can make its construction sector fairer and more transparent, reducing corruption and boosting economic growth.

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.source: Regional Lens
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.source: Gestion et management public
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: A Policy Analysis of PFAS Regulations in Maine and the US Federal Government
government.short_title: A Policy Analysis of PFAS Regulations in Maine and the US Federal Government
government.source: Maine Policy Review
government.plain_summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are harmful chemicals found in many products that have contaminated the environment. The US government has not uniformly addressed PFAS issues, but some states like Maine have taken strong actions. Maine has implemented various measures such as education, labeling requirements, and bans on certain agricultural practices. They also have unique regulations like banning the use of PFAS in food products like beef, dairy, and eggs.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.source: International Journal of Government Auditing
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.source: International Journal of Government Auditing
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.source: Gestion et management public
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.source: Gestion et management public
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: Does gender matter in combating corruption? A comparative analysis of Chinese manufacturing companies
government.short_title: Does gender matter in combating corruption? A comparative analysis of Chinese manufacturing co…
government.source: Feminist Encounters: A Journal of Critical Studies in Culture and Politics
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how attitudes towards cooperation with others affect efforts to stop bribery in manufacturing companies in China. It found that having a cooperative attitude helps employees resist unethical behaviors like bribery. Importantly, the research showed that women play a bigger role in reducing unethical attitudes among employees compared to men. This highlights the importance of considering gender when creating ethical policies and practices.

government.short_title: Vertical and horizontal accountability: determinants of government transparency in China

government.title: The Production Process of Gold Mining, Corruption, Weak Regulatory Institutions, and Development in Cameroon
government.short_title: The Production Process of Gold Mining, Corruption, Weak Regulatory Institutions, and Developme…
government.source: Advances in Social Sciences Research Journal
government.plain_summary: Gold mining in Cameroon is rich in deposits but faces major governance issues, leading to little economic benefit. Despite having significant gold reserves, the sector struggles with corruption, weak regulatory systems, and illegal financial activities. This causes discrepancies between what Cameroon officially reports and what other countries record, with over 95% of gold output going through informal channels. To address these issues, there needs to be stronger enforcement of regulations, better supply chain tracking, and cooperation between different government agencies.

government.title: Assessing the Impact of the Whistleblower Protection Act on Corruption Mitigation and Institutional Accountability in India
government.short_title: Assessing the Impact of the Whistleblower Protection Act on Corruption Mitigation and Institut…
government.source: Pacific Journal of Modern Theories and Research
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how the Whistleblower Protection Act in India has helped reduce corruption and improved how institutions are held accountable. While the act is a step in the right direction, it hasn't been fully effective because of issues like lack of enforcement and changes that weakened some protections. The study found that while whistleblowers have gained some power, there's still a lot of work to be done to make the system more robust. It suggests that for the act to be more effective, there needs to be stronger mechanisms for reporting wrongdoings, quicker resolutions, and support for whistleblowers.

government.title: Analysis of Accountability, Transparency and Internal Control over the Management of Village Fund Allocations in the Village Government of Klurak Candi Sidoarjo
government.short_title: Analysis of Accountability, Transparency and Internal Control over the Management of Village F…
government.source: Indonesian Journal of Law and Economics Review
government.plain_summary: This study examines how the Klurak Village Government manages Village Fund Allocation, focusing on accountability, transparency, and internal control. It found that accountability is implemented through planning, implementation, administration, reporting, and ensuring responsibilities are met. The study also noted that budget information is made public through various means like BPD involvement, information boards, and social media. However, the inactive village website limits the public's access to financial information.

government.title: Anti-Corruption Agencies Effort In Curbing Bureaucratic Corruption In Adamawa State From 2013-2023
government.short_title: Anti-Corruption Agencies Effort In Curbing Bureaucratic Corruption In Adamawa State From 2013-…
government.source: ADSU International Journal of Politics, Administration and Management (AIJPAM)
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how anti-corruption agencies worked to reduce corruption in Adamawa State, Nigeria. They used surveys to gather data from 380 people. The study found that having good policies and strong structures helps create effective strategies to fight corruption. Collaboration among different groups also plays a big role in making these strategies work.

government.title: Impact of Audit Independence and Accountability in Zamfara State Public Sector
government.short_title: Impact of Audit Independence and Accountability in Zamfara State Public Sector
government.source: JOURNAL OF ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how much independence auditors have in Zamfara State's public sector and how that affects their accountability. They used two measures: how much the auditors are paid and how long they stay. Higher pay and longer stays were linked to better financial reporting. The study suggests that the government should use fair bidding processes for hiring auditors and have clear fee structures to avoid overpaying which could compromise the auditors' independence.

government.title: Forensic Auditing and Financial Strength Transparency in Selected Southwest Government Sector of Nigeria
government.short_title: Forensic Auditing and Financial Strength Transparency in Selected Southwest Government Sector…
government.source: JOURNAL OF ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how forensic auditing can improve financial transparency in government sectors in Southwest Nigeria. Forensic auditing includes techniques like investigating financial issues, analyzing evidence, and providing support in legal cases. The study found that forensic auditing can make financial information more open, clear, and accessible. Specifically, investigative techniques and evidence analysis help make financial information more open.

government.title: How digital portfolios become governable: a venture design research study of public sector digital development
government.short_title: How digital portfolios become governable: a venture design research study of public sector dig…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study explores how public sector organizations can better govern digital development projects. It suggests that instead of relying on existing tools, digital solutions should be designed to make governance more visible, comparable, and subject to collective decision-making. The research found that by actively specifying governance through design, digital solutions can lead to more transparent discussions and decisions. However, long-term outcomes like strategic alignment and public value creation are harder to measure.

government.title: Responsible AI beyond compliance: governing everyday use in the public sector
government.short_title: Responsible AI beyond compliance: governing everyday use in the public sector
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public sector organizations manage the use of AI, focusing on how they align everyday practices with governance and accountability requirements. Despite formal structures, employees often use AI in ways that don't align with these structures, leading to a governance-practice gap. To address this, governance evolves through various mechanisms like technical controls, human oversight, and informal guidance. The findings suggest that AI use doesn't replace human judgement but rather intensifies it, requiring more verification and training.

government.title: Data Spaces - Public Sector Implementation of Sovereign Data Collaboration
government.short_title: Data Spaces - Public Sector Implementation of Sovereign Data Collaboration
government.source: Digital Government: Research and Practice
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how governments can collaborate securely on data, especially in a world where data ownership is important. It looks at how public sector organizations in Germany are setting up controlled environments for sharing data, like the Gaia-X initiative. The study found that for these data spaces to work well, organizations need to have strong capabilities, be innovative, and trust each other. It's also important to have clear standards and good governance.

government.title: Corruption in the health sector in contexts of health crises: An exploratory analysis
government.short_title: Corruption in the health sector in contexts of health crises: An exploratory analysis
government.source: Public Health of Indonesia
government.plain_summary: This study examines corruption in the health sector during health crises in Colombia using administrative data. It found that some departments awarded contracts with very high values compared to their duration, which could indicate corruption. The research used statistical methods to identify unusual patterns in contract awards. These findings suggest that data analysis can help detect potential corruption in public health procurement.

government.title: Strategic Approaches to Anti-Corruption: An Analysis of the Initiatives and Effectiveness of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) in Nigeria
government.short_title: Strategic Approaches to Anti-Corruption: An Analysis of the Initiatives and Effectiveness of t…
government.source: International Journal of Education, Culture, and Society
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how the ICPC in Nigeria is fighting corruption. The ICPC has been trying to improve transparency and accountability through audits, public campaigns, and other measures. While they've made some progress, they face big challenges like not having enough money, political interference, and weak cooperation with other agencies. Corruption still persists because people don't follow rules voluntarily.

government.title: Whistle-Blowing Policy and Anti-Corruption War in Nigeria, 2016-2024
government.short_title: Whistle-Blowing Policy and Anti-Corruption War in Nigeria, 2016-2024
government.source: International Journal of Education, Culture, and Society
government.plain_summary: Corruption is a big problem in Nigeria that affects how well the government works and how people feel about their government. In 2016, the government started a policy called the Whistle-Blowing Policy to encourage people to report when they see corruption. This policy helped find and recover some of the money that was stolen from the government. However, the policy didn't work as well as it could because the government wasn't fully supporting it.

government.title: Impact of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) Adoption on Financial Transparency in the Nigerian Public Sector
government.short_title: Impact of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) Adoption on Financial Trans…
government.source: JOURNAL OF ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how adopting International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) in Nigeria improved financial transparency in the public sector. It surveyed 400 public sector officials across different levels of government to see how well they disclosed financial information. The study found that when IPSAS was adopted, financial transparency, disclosure quality, accountability, and comparability all improved. IPSAS also seemed to reduce corruption.

government.title: Corruption and Human Rights Violations: The Role of Local Government in Curbing Corruption and Its Effects on Citizens’ Access to Rights
government.short_title: Corruption and Human Rights Violations: The Role of Local Government in Curbing Corruption and…
government.source: The Strategic Review for Southern Africa
government.plain_summary: Local governments are supposed to deliver essential services and uphold human rights, but often struggle with corruption, weak controls, and institutional capture. This can lead to inequality and undermine the rule of law. The article looks at how corruption affects human rights in South Africa and suggests that strong anti-corruption systems can improve rights outcomes. It found that in some localities, like Midvaal, these systems can make a difference, while others like Madibeng show how corruption can lead to specific human rights violations.

government.title: Prospects for the development of anti-corruption policy in the Russian Federation.
government.short_title: Prospects for the development of anti-corruption policy in the Russian Federation.
government.source: UPRAVLENIE / MANAGEMENT (Russia)
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how Russia is trying to fight corruption. It uses various methods like making laws and training people to prevent corruption. The effectiveness of these methods is being studied. The study found that reducing corruption involves limiting power, making procedures more transparent, and holding officials accountable.

government.title: Systemic Imbalances in Integrity Management Systems: A Meso‐Level Framework From Four Corruption Scandals
government.short_title: Systemic Imbalances in Integrity Management Systems: A Meso‐Level Framework From Four Corrupti…
government.source: Regulation & Governance
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how integrity management systems (IMSs) are used to promote ethical conduct and prevent corruption. Despite their promotion, there's little understanding of how these systems work in practice. The study developed a framework that looks at four key areas: belief, boundary, diagnostic, and interaction systems of control. It analyzed four major corruption cases in different sectors like infrastructure, healthcare, banking, and defense.

government.title: Legislative Oversight and Public Accountability in Indonesia’s Strategic Sector Governance: An Administrative Governance Perspective
government.short_title: Legislative Oversight and Public Accountability in Indonesia’s Strategic Sector Governance: An…
government.source: Green Social: International Journal of Law and Civil Affairs
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how the Indonesian House of Representatives, specifically Commission VII, oversees strategic sectors like industry, tourism, and media. It identifies four main challenges in this oversight, such as not having enough information, unclear responsibilities, not following up on recommendations, and politics influencing the process. To address these issues, the study proposes a framework called LOAA, which includes gathering information, evaluating performance, assessing public value, giving corrective advice, and ensuring follow-up. This framework can help improve how the government manages these important sectors and ensure they are run responsibly.

government.title: Transparent budget: the idea of deep transparency
government.short_title: Transparent budget: the idea of deep transparency
government.source: Public Sector Economics
government.plain_summary: Transparent budgeting means governments know exactly where public money goes, but citizens often don't. This paper suggests a new way to make spending transparent so citizens can see every penny goes to the right person. It uses special technology like WORM storage and blockchain to connect where money is allocated to where it's actually spent. This makes it harder for people to misuse public funds, like giving favors or stealing money.

government.title: An Iterative Framework for AI Adoption in the Public Sector: Insights from a Swiss Case Study
government.short_title: An Iterative Framework for AI Adoption in the Public Sector: Insights from a Swiss Case Study
government.source: JeDEM - eJournal of eDemocracy and Open Government
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how to use AI in public sector projects, specifically in a Swiss healthcare cost verification chatbot. The research found that using an iterative framework helped navigate challenges and made the AI system more user-friendly. By doing many small improvements and getting feedback, they could keep the project moving forward even when faced with public sector constraints. This framework helped the team learn and adapt, leading to better AI systems that could be used in government.

government.title: Real-Time Internal Control Dynamics and Fraud Prevention: A Framework for Strengthening Financial Integrity in Public Sectors
government.short_title: Real-Time Internal Control Dynamics and Fraud Prevention: A Framework for Strengthening Financ…
government.source: International Review of Management and Marketing
government.plain_summary: This study focuses on improving financial integrity in the Nigerian public sector by examining how real-time internal control practices can prevent fraud. It found that real-time authorisation significantly reduces unauthorized activities and enhances compliance. Periodic checks also help in detecting irregularities promptly. However, biometric authentication like fingerprint scanning and facial recognition did not show a clear benefit in this context.

government.title: The Role of Ethics in the Implementation of Anti-Corruption Standards for Civil Servants in Russia and China
government.short_title: The Role of Ethics in the Implementation of Anti-Corruption Standards for Civil Servants in Ru…
government.source: Public International and Private International Law
government.plain_summary: Corruption damages trust in government by civil servants. To fight it effectively, we need strong ethical standards alongside institutional changes. Russia and China have taken different approaches to this; studying their methods can help create better systems globally. Understanding both universal principles and cultural specifics is key for creating effective anti-corruption measures.

nonprofit.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

nonprofit.title: The New Middle Class of Iran and the Demand for Reforming Domestic and Foreign Political Relations
nonprofit.short_title: The New Middle Class of Iran and the Demand for Reforming Domestic and Foreign Political Relat…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
nonprofit.plain_summary: The new middle class in Iran grew significantly after the Islamic Revolution and played a key role in pushing for reforms in both domestic and foreign policies. This group became more active in elections over time, aiming to influence how the government handled these areas. Despite their efforts through voting, they haven't been able to fully change the system's approach to politics internationally or domestically. Their success was mainly seen in getting more people involved in electoral processes.

nonprofit.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
nonprofit.short_title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Inte…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research evaluates Iran's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to see how well it supports responsible use of AI. The strategy emphasizes values like human dignity and national priorities, but lacks clear plans for key areas like funding, data access, and regulation. To succeed, the strategy needs more specific details on these aspects. Practitioners should focus not just on ethical principles, but also on practical steps to ensure AI is used responsibly and effectively in Iran.

nonprofit.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
nonprofit.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
nonprofit.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
nonprofit.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

nonprofit.title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary After Indonesian Constitutional Court Decision No. 66/PUU-XXIV/2026: A Fiqh Siyasah Perspective
nonprofit.short_title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary…
nonprofit.source: JISRev: Journal of Islamic Studies Review
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research looks at the difference between maladministration and corruption, using a specific case about buying Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia. It found four key factors to decide if something is corruption: whether someone intended to do wrong, if they got personal benefit from it, if money was lost as a result, and if proper steps were taken afterward. The study also suggests that when all these factors are met, what started as maladministration can be considered corruption. However, the research points out there should be an initial check by a special committee before going to criminal courts.

nonprofit.title: Strategic Approaches to Anti-Corruption: An Analysis of the Initiatives and Effectiveness of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) in Nigeria
nonprofit.short_title: Strategic Approaches to Anti-Corruption: An Analysis of the Initiatives and Effectiveness of t…
nonprofit.source: International Journal of Education, Culture, and Society
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how the ICPC in Nigeria is fighting corruption. The ICPC has been trying to improve transparency and accountability through audits, public campaigns, and other measures. While they've made some progress, they face big challenges like not having enough money, political interference, and weak cooperation with other agencies. Corruption still persists because people don't follow rules voluntarily.
